thread:
maya: heads-up — after the kernel-selection change in staging (#kernel-hint=prefer_fused) I'm seeing sustained +1.2GB GPU memory compared to master for 8-shard TP runs. pattern looks like repeated tempbuf spikes during forward where nccl/allreduce is invoked. attaching quick nvprof dump below.

maya: nvprof snippet (trimmed):
```
Time(%)  Total Time  Calls  Avg Time  Min Time  Max Time  Name
 12.4    1.2s       48    25ms      2ms       48ms      cudaMalloc (temp)
 15.8    1.5s       96    15.6ms    1.2ms     34ms      ncclAllReduce (kernel)
  8.6    0.8s       96    8.3ms     0.8ms     20ms      memcpy HtoD
```

maya: the key weirdness is the allocator churn: a bunch of cudaMalloc/free for ephemeral workspaces around the comm call. not persistent tensors.

arjun: hmm — did the kernel selector flip us to the fused-attn kernel that requests a dynamic workspace per-call? we saw that pattern with the new fused kernels where workspace_size() can be large and per-call.

arjun: can you paste the kernel introspect output for the problematic batch? i want to see workspace_size() estimates.

maya: pasted from the model runtime log (trimmed):
```
[kernel-select] chosen=attn_fused_1, workspace_bytes=2097152, temp_allocs=3
[comm] nccl_phase=allreduce, comm_tmp=1048576
[alloc] fallback_malloc for comm_tmp (cudaMalloc) size=1048576
```

ivan: KV cache could be contributing to fragmentation — if we frequently allocate ephemeral buffers between kv-cache persistence windows the allocator may fragment and trigger cudaMallocs. did you try running with our slabbased allocator pinning turned on?

maya: yes — with slabbased pinned arena it's slightly better (~600MB overhead vs 1.2GB) but still spikey. the pattern correlates with number of micro-batches (higher micro-batches => more small temp allocs).

liz: ran a narrow benchmark on gpux-08 with 8TP shards. numbers:
- master (old kernel-selector, arena pinned): steady mem 22.1GB, peak 22.6GB
- kernel-hint=prefer_fused (arena pinned): steady mem 23.0GB, peak 24.2GB
- kernel-hint=prefer_fused + workspace-cache (experimental): steady mem 22.4GB, peak 22.9GB

liz: workspace-cache = keep a single cudaMalloc'd workspace per kernel variant per device and reuse for subsequent calls. seems to remove most of the repeated cudaMalloc churn. implementation was hacky but shows the value.

arjun: nice. that suggests we should do two things: (1) prefer reusing a persistent per-kernel workspace where safe, (2) adjust kernel selection heuristic to prefer kernel variants that declare smaller dynamic workspace when micro-batches > 1.

ivan: +1 on both. also propose we add a small pooling layer for NCCL comm buffers: preallocate a small slab for nccl temp buffers per device sized to max(comm_tmp) observed in a rolling window. that reduces cudaMallocs and keeps fragmentation lower.

maya: will try implementing per-device comm-slab (size heuristic: 2x 95th percentile comm_tmp over last 5 minutes, capped at 256MB). quick prototype locally reduced peak by 900MB.

perf-bot: perf/regression: memory-peak increased by +4.3% on staging (1850011000 -> 1850011100), test: tp_infer_smoke_8shard, owner: maya

maya: thanks perf-bot. action items:
- maya: prototype comm-slab + workspace-cache (WIP)
- arjun: add kernel selection fallback that considers workspace_bytes when recommending fused kernels
- ivan: run fragmentation stress with KV cache churn + micro-batches to validate slab heuristics
- liz: run multi-run benchmark and collect nvprof + allocator trace (malloc/free counts)

liz: one more datapoint — enabling async memcpy for comm path reduced walltime variance but didn't change peak memory. so this is allocator-pattern memory, not GPU memcpy backlog.

arjun: for rollout safest path is: workspace-cache opt-in flag + comm-slab behind feature flag + metrics exposed in console (alloc/free rate, slab misses, workspace reassignments). then enable in canary.

maya: agreed. i'll open a draft PR with the workspace-cache prototype and a perf dashboard draft. tagging @eng-runtime for visibility.

ivan: if anyone hits OOM during dogfooding, set env REDWOOD_COMM_SLAB=off or REDWOOD_WORKSPACE_CACHE=off to revert quickly.

maya: will post PR link when ready. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
